title: R2 serves simulations straight from the bucket, bypassing /sim-public — no boot snippet, no CSP frame-ancestors, no revision publication gate
Under R2 the sim-public binary redirect targets /hls-proxy, whose scope check 403s a simulations/ key — every .glb fails
SIM_PREPARE_TIMEOUT_MS is a shared 5s constant; a 29.7MB model load cannot make it and 3 failures open the session breaker
Package weight never reaches pool tier, residency capacity or prepare budget — tier 'all' mounts 4 packages on device signals alone
sim_revisions.metadata is queried with unguarded `jsonb - text`; a scalar row throws 22023 and aborts project duplication
storePoster writes variants through the drizzle jsonb codec against a jsonb_typeof='array' CHECK, and no test exercises that pair
sim_meta.runtimeValidated is written false by both paths, set true by nothing, and read by nothing
Container capture requires a /sim-public/ key in the served URL — the R2 cutover demotes every sim export to a poster
Capture staging materialises the whole package as Buffers in the Node heap, bounded only at 256MiB and checked after the read
The residency lead window excludes document load and is clamped at 10s — the cost that dominates a 35MB package is invisible to it
checkReplaceCompatibility degenerates towards always-compatible against a 715KB minified bundle
R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/R2_PUBLIC_URL unset silently yields root-relative sim URLs instead of failing at boot
Comment claims /sim-public/* calls the media gate; it does not — security-005 is still open and now reads as closed
stack.md and the reviewer brief describe SimBridgeContract.ts as the wire protocol; it is the replace-compatibility checker
RUM records no document-load duration and no package weight, so the field cannot distinguish a slow fetch from a slow prepare
